# Job #57: STM32H743 AIO Flight Controller with 4-in-1 80A ESC

## Electro-Thermal Model, DShot DMA Allocation, and Reference Netlist

---

## 0. Architecture Clarification and Feasibility Flags

Two points need settling before any math, because they change the design.

**1. The H743 does not commutate the motors.** ArduPilot runs on the H743 as the flight controller and sends bi-directional DShot600 to four dedicated ESC MCUs. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by those ESC MCUs, which run AM32 or BLHeli_32-class firmware. The reference design uses an AT32F421 or STM32G071 per ESC channel. This document therefore models two separate domains:

- **FC domain (H743):** DShot600 generation and eRPM telemetry capture via DMA.
- **Power domain (4× ESC MCU + gate driver + 24 MOSFETs):** conduction and switching losses at 48 kHz.

**2. 80A is a burst rating, not a continuous one, on a nano form factor.** As shown in §3, 4 × 80A on a 20×20 or 25.5×25.5 mm board dissipates about 85–95 W. The board can sustain that for only **about 2–4 seconds** before reaching thermal limits. The deliverable is therefore a *time-limited burst model*, and the firmware must enforce it (see §3.5).

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Temperature-dependent R_DS(on)

$$
R_{DS(on)}(T_J) = R_{DS(on),25}\,\big[1 + \alpha\,(T_J - 25)\big], \quad \alpha \approx 0.005\text{–}0.007\ \text{K}^{-1}
$$

At T_J = 110 °C with α = 0.006, the multiplier is 1.51:

$$
R_{hot} \approx 1.5\ \text{m}\Omega
$$

This positive feedback (hotter FET → higher R → more loss) is why the burst model in §3 must be iterated rather than solved once.

### 1.2 Current path in six-step with synchronous rectification

At any commutation step, one phase is high, one is low, and one is floating.

- The **non-PWM leg** stays fully on, either its HS or LS FET depending on the scheme.
- The **PWM leg** alternates between HS and LS. With complementary PWM, current flows through whichever FET is on during each part of the period. Current never rests in the body diode except during dead time.

The motor current therefore always flows through **exactly two channel resistances in series**, independent of duty cycle D:

$$
P_{cond,motor} = I_{RMS}^2 \cdot 2R_{hot}
$$

### 1.3 Ripple correction

The PWM leg carries a triangular ripple ΔI on top of the DC current:

$$
I_{RMS}^2 = I_{avg}^2 + \frac{\Delta I^2}{12}, \qquad
\Delta I = \frac{(V_{bus} - V_{bemf})\,D}{L_{ph\text{-}ph}\,f_{sw}}
$$

Example: a 2306 motor with L_ph-ph ≈ 15 µH, at high throttle where V_bus − V_bemf ≈ 3 V and D ≈ 0.9:

$$
\Delta I = \frac{3 \cdot 0.9}{15\times10^{-6}\cdot 48\times10^3} = 3.75\ \text{A}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\frac{\Delta I^2}{12} = 1.17\ \text{A}^2
$$

This is negligible against 6400 A². Note that the correction becomes significant at low duty with low-inductance motors, which is one argument for 48 kHz over 24 kHz.

### 1.4 Numbers at 80 A burst

| Term | Expression | Value |
|---|---|---|
| FET conduction per motor | 80² × 2 × 1.5 mΩ | **19.2 W** |
| Per-FET average (each FET conducts 1/3 of the electrical cycle) | 19.2 W ÷ 6 FETs | ≈ 3.2 W |
| Per-FET *instantaneous* while conducting | 80² × 1.5 mΩ | 9.6 W |
| PCB copper (phase + bus path, ≈ 0.4 mΩ round trip, hot) | 80² × 0.4 mΩ | 2.6 W |
| Current-sense shunt (0.25 mΩ, single-shunt topology) | 80² × 0.25 mΩ | 1.6 W per ESC channel if per-channel shunt |

**Key point:** the 9.6 W instantaneous loss matters for thermal ripple at low eRPM. Below roughly 1000 eRPM a single FET can carry the full current for milliseconds, which approaches its Z_θJC transient time constant. This is the "hot start / stalled motor" failure mode. It must be handled by a stall/desync current limit, not by the steady-state burst budget.

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

Only the **PWM leg** switches. Each PWM period contains one turn-on and one turn-off of the active FET. In the complementary leg, the synchronous FET switches at near-zero V_DS (ZVS) because the body diode conducts during dead time first.

### 2.1 Hard-switching V–I overlap

Switching transition time is dominated by the Miller plateau:

$$
t_{sw} \approx \frac{Q_{gd}}{I_{gate}}, \quad
I_{gate,on} \approx \frac{V_{drv} - V_{plateau}}{R_{g,ext}+R_{g,int}+R_{drv}}
$$

With V_drv = 10 V, V_plateau ≈ 4 V, and R_total ≈ 6 Ω, I_gate ≈ 1 A and t_r ≈ t_f ≈ 10 ns. The design value uses **15 ns** each to cover layout inductance and current-limited driver behavior.

$$
P_{VI} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,V_{bus}\,I\,(t_r + t_f)\,f_{sw}
= 0.5 \cdot 25.2 \cdot 80 \cdot 30\times10^{-9} \cdot 48\times10^3
= \mathbf{1.45\ W}
$$

### 2.2 Reverse recovery of the complementary body diode

$$
P_{rr} = Q_{rr}\,V_{bus}\,f_{sw} = 40\times10^{-9}\cdot25.2\cdot48\times10^3 = 0.048\ \text{W}
$$

Q_rr rises roughly linearly with I_F and dI/dt, so derate by 2× at 80 A, giving **≈ 0.10 W**.

### 2.3 Output capacitance (C_oss) energy

$$
P_{oss} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,Q_{oss}\,V_{bus}\,f_{sw} = 0.5\cdot40\times10^{-9}\cdot25.2\cdot48\times10^3 = 0.024\ \text{W}
$$

### 2.4 Dead-time body-diode conduction

There are two dead-time intervals per period:

$$
P_{dt} = V_F\,I\,(2t_{dt})\,f_{sw} = 0.8\cdot80\cdot100\times10^{-9}\cdot48\times10^3 = \mathbf{0.31\ W}
$$

### 2.5 Gate drive

This loss is dissipated mostly in the driver and gate resistors, not the FETs. Two FETs (HS + LS of the PWM leg) are driven:

$$
P_{gate} = 2\,Q_g\,V_{drv}\,f_{sw} = 2\cdot50\times10^{-9}\cdot10\cdot48\times10^3 = 0.048\ \text{W}
$$

### 2.6 Switching summary per motor at 80 A, 25.2 V

| Component | W |
|---|---|
| V–I overlap | 1.45 |
| Reverse recovery (derated) | 0.10 |
| C_oss | 0.02 |
| Dead-time diode | 0.31 |
| Gate (driver-side) | 0.05 |
| **Total switching** | **≈ 1.93 W** |
